scope: Continue PAR-92/7BA by indexing child-first orphan identity so a late parent cannot adopt a vertex whose observed owner differs, while preserving that orphan for its actual owner.

implementation.inverseIndex: The existing ordered handle-to-owner claim index now also supports single orphan-owner claims. The reader keeps a separate inverse index for staged orphan vertices and rejects foreign ownership in logarithmic lookup over a late parent's deduplicated declared-child index.
implementation.arrivalOrder: If the child arrives first under owner A and a later parent B declares that child, B is rejected before pending-state insertion; the orphan remains available for A. If B is already pending when an A-owned child arrives, the pre-existing reverse-claim path terminalizes B and rejects the child, preserving the existing conflict outcome across arrival order.
implementation.lifecycle: Inverse claims are registered with orphan staging and removed on same-owner adoption, orphan terminalization, pending-owner terminalization, and final abandonment. The shared staging ledger charges inverse-index nodes, preflights the extra claim charge with vector growth and per-owner membership, and validates index/state correspondence and exact modeled-byte totals.

charged: inverse ordered-map child-key and owner-set node estimates
orphan vector capacities and per-owner child-handle membership nodes
the existing declared-child, pending-vector, and parent-claim charges
notCharged: top-level pending/orphan unordered-map buckets and nodes
budget.qualification: An explicit retained-state budget estimate, not an RSS cap.

cases: 512 declared child handles with a matching orphan owner remain admissible
a foreign late parent is rejected by the inverse owner lookup
lookup work stays below 512*16 ordered comparisons
duplicate owner insertion refuses without mutating the charge or index
claim removal returns exact modeled bytes and leaves the index empty
one-byte budget refusal leaves no partial index or output charge
existing vector/map growth, membership, and competing-parent claim controls remain green
